card_notes.text: Pim knows Corbin is leaving at the end of the week.

characters.name: Pim Tallowby
characters.appearance: Short and round-cheeked, with freckles, brown hair in a flour-dusted braid and a tiny copper bell in one ear.
characters.sketch: A chatty, curious baker's apprentice who is always slightly behind and mostly forgiven.

wants.text: to keep everything exactly as it is

characters.fear: Being the reason something goes wrong.
characters.flaw: She says yes to everything, then panics.

values.text: caring for the people she feeds

behaviors.tendency: go quiet and tidy everything in reach

characters.competence: Can tell the weather by how dough rises.
characters.vulnerability: She cannot say no to anyone who asks kindly.
characters.speech: Chatty and quick, trailing off into questions.

characters.name: Orla Fennick
characters.appearance: Tall and wiry, with cropped white hair and forearms scarred from the oven.
characters.sketch: A gruff, fair master baker who shows rather than tells.

wants.text: to carry on exactly as she always has

characters.flaw: She will not explain anything she cannot show by doing.
characters.competence: Reads fire and heat by feel.
characters.vulnerability: She cannot bear being thought past it.
characters.history: Has fired the same oven every morning for forty years.

characters.name: Corbin Reeds
characters.appearance: Lanky, with ink-stained thumbs, a sunburnt neck and a feathered hat he is very proud of.
characters.sketch: A delighted wanderer who maps the world but never stays in it.
characters.flaw: He leaves before things get hard.
characters.competence: Draws a true map from a single walk.
characters.vulnerability: He cannot resist an unexplored road.
characters.speech: Talks a lot and wanders off mid-sentence.
characters.history: Has spent ten years walking from valley to valley.

world.name: Thimble Hollow
world.era_and_technology: A small valley village of lamps, carts and hand tools, with no telephones or engines.
world.everyday_life: Bread is the village's whole economy, and applewood is rationed because the orchard is sick, so every market ends in an argument over fuel.
world.history: The village grew up around its oven, which was built before the first houses.

places.name: The bakery
places.description: A warm, low building at the village center with the oven at its heart.
places.effect: People linger and tell secrets they meant to keep.

places.name: The Millpond
places.description: A still pond at the edge of the village.
places.effect: Nobody ever raises their voice there.

objects.name: The Weather Oven
objects.description: A huge black brick oven in the bakery.
objects.significance: Whatever is baked in it settles the next three days of weather.

objects.name: Mother's Starter
objects.description: A two-hundred-year-old sourdough culture kept in a crock in the cellar.
objects.significance: Every loaf in the valley descends from it.

powers.name: The Parish Council
powers.nature: Five elders who set the dates of the village's festivals and fairs.
powers.hold: They can appoint or dismiss the baker.
powers.felt: Most people only meet them as notices nailed to the well.

rules.statement: The Weather Oven works only when fired with applewood.
rules.cost: Every winter the village rations the orchard to keep the oven fed.
rules.when_broken: If anyone fires it with other wood, the weather is said to turn.

terms.meaning: a weather forecast baked into bread
